title: One night in the ward | वार्ड में एक रात
look: Rukavat: a 1980s family-TV magazine look (soft gouache, warm paper grain, rounded TV-screen corners on establishing shots) laid over a present-day district hospital: steel drip stands, blue plastic chairs, green cloth curtains, tube lights, phones. Every painting: no words, no letters, no numbers, nothing written; signs, papers and screens painted blank or shut; unsigned; heads 30 to 45 percent down; a plain wall or sky beside each speaker; the player never shown (no face, hand, sleeve or shadow); card people never painted.
goals: Turns, jobs: slept 6 or more | बारी, काम: नींद 6 या ज़्यादा  (every night turn and morning job to someone who slept 6 hours or more last night; fed by the plain Split twin, D1 and D5, set A)

Cots, taxi seats: on feet 12 or more | खाट, टैक्सी सीटें: खड़े 12 या ज़्यादा  (every cot and taxi seat to someone on their feet 12 hours or more today; fed by the plain Spend checks twin, D4 and D8, set A)
Fixed line for the matters twin (D3, D7), the same for everyone: Doctor: answered. Mama ji: told. | डॉक्टर: जवाब। मामा जी: ख़बर।
Stamp on Rukavat's interruption card: Nani home: 10:00 (both targets met) / 11:00 (one) / 12:30 (none) | नानी घर: 10:00 / 11:00 / 12:30

Rukavat look over a present-day district hospital at night seen from the road: a plain two-storey building, one lit window upstairs, a blank cream board above the gate painted flat, a row of parked scooters with plain number plates, no people. Calm space: the dark blue sky across the top half, where the title sits. [BREAKS rules 25 and 50: the home chapter carries one hard topic, not the two you chose on 22 Oct (dowry the second); the bible moves dowry to the wedding chapter] [WAITS rulebook Q3]. writer_notes: BREAKS rule 15 (no tie between two women or two men on any of the 8 decisions). Why: each person keeps the same numbers wherever a set shows, and each set carries 4 equal pairs among 10 people, so the 2 left over in each set are a woman and a man (set A: Yasmin and Nagsen; set B: Mumtaz and Nagsen). Two women or two men can then share numbers only by copying a pair's numbers, which rule 17's last clause forbids, and every set-B decision is a pick one, where the lowest pair needs both spares below it. A solver run over all 144 pair plans that keep rules 13, 17 and 21 found no line-up with even one such tie. Ways out, for you or the research side: 12 people a circle (rule 11 says 8 to 10), a Rank or Team decision in set B so the pair is not always on top, or let a spare share a pair's numbers (marked as a rule 17 break).

BREAKS rule 17, weakest: Ganga is the weakest card in D5 (on her feet 15 hours, slept 2) and sits in D8's pair. Of all the line-ups the solver found, none kept every weakest card out of later pairs while also matching each pair's earlier showings; this was the single break left. The same tiredness that makes her weakest for a morning job makes her most deserving of a seat in D8.

BREAKS rule 17, warmth (2 pairs): in D4, Uma's bottom-half showing carried a heavy fact (D2, unwell since the winter fever) where Dinesh's carried a warm one (D3, fixed Nani's fan); in D7, Rajan's carried a judging note (D1, moody) where Uma's matching showing (D4) carried a plain one. The halves (top or bottom) match for every pair, measured as chapter 3's checker measures them (more cards beaten than beating, over both numbers).

BREAKS rule 17, age: in twin C (the matters twin, D3 and D7) the man is older in both halves (Yasmin 32 with Firoz 40; Uma 34 with Rajan 40). The circle has only three woman-older pairs (Ganga twice, Mumtaz with Firoz) and the hard twin and both plain twins need them, so the one break is on the twin whose reason may fairly be followed both times.

BREAKS rule 21 (from the bible's circle): Nagsen is on five cards and never in a pair, since no woman in the circle has a Marathi name, and the one-pair names (Yasmin, Mumtaz) plus Nagsen are the only cards free to be the weakest early on (rule 17). So a community-marked name is the weakest card in 5 of the 7 decisions that have a weakest card (Nagsen in D1, D2 and D6, Yasmin in D4, Mumtaz in D7). Counted by places instead, marked names hold 3 of the 6 top places and 6 of the 13 bottom places, near their 40% share. Nagsen gets one top place (D8) and one warm note (D7). The fix sits in the bible: give Nagsen a Marathi-named woman to pair with, or put the never-paired card on a name that marks no community.

BREAKS rules 25 and 50 (as the bible marks): the home chapter carries one hard topic, not two; WAITS rulebook Q3. If the answer is two, twin D (the cots and seats) turns hard with the bible's care facts, and the counts here change.

BREAKS rule 18 (as the bible marks): 9 sets in the take; WAITS options Q8. CHANGED from the bible: set B's second number was 'km away from the hospital', but every card person is Nani's neighbour from one lane, so it would be the same for all. It is now 'Years known: years they have known Nani' (पहचान), capped at each person's age minus 6. Native readers choose the final key words.

CLASH rules 26 and 36: the title card must name the setting ('a quarrel over a house') before Start, and rule 36 bars any earlier line from using a coming card's note words, so the two hard notes avoid 'quarrel', 'house', 'घर' and 'झगड़ा'. A script (ch2_notecheck.py) scans every story line, question, slot label and button before each decision for the content words of that decision's notes; it is clean. Kin names used as names (Nani) are not counted as content words.

STORY LOGIC flag: the cards' numbers are the visitor slips filled in at the gate at 9 pm, so in the morning decisions (D5 at 6:00, D8 at 8:30) 'slept last night' and 'on feet today' are still the evening's figures. A careful player may notice. Options: relabel set A 'on feet by 9 pm' and 'slept the night before' in this chapter, or give the morning twins a second slip.

CHANGED pairs (the bible allows it; the checker should prove the new set): D1 Deepa and Rajan, D2 Ganga and Dinesh, D3 Yasmin and Firoz, D4 Uma and Dinesh, D5 Mumtaz and Firoz, D6 Deepa and Sunil, D7 Uma and Rajan, D8 Ganga and Sunil. Why: the bible's set put the man older in both halves of a plain twin (A), and its warmth and earlier-showing history could not be matched. Kept: one pair per set per person, at most two pairs each, never two decisions running, no repeat, within 8 years, Muslim names only with Muslim names, no hard fact on a community-marked name, first-half nudge on the man in A and D and on the woman in B and C, as the bible's take-wide count needs.

CHANGED hard facts (rule 28): the bible had the quarrel with 'her brother' and 'his brother'. A daughter claiming her father's house and a son doing so do not read the same in many homes, so each quarrels with a sibling of the same sex: Ganga fell out with her sister over their father's home (D2); Sunil is estranged from his brother over the family home (D6). Hindi: अनबन against मनमुटाव. For the five Hindi-first readers. No court or legal claim (rule 29); a neighbour's own case, never the household's (rule 27).

CHANGED the taxi decision (D8) from 9:30 at the gate to 8:30 at the taxi stand, booked for whenever Nani is let go, because a stamp of 'Nani home: 11:00' or '12:30' cannot follow a taxi already at the gate at 9:30 (rule 43: every decision happens before the outcome).

Nudges and notes: rules 19, 20 and 22 hold by script. Notes in each decision are within 2 words of each other in each language, the pair's two notes are the same length, the longest note sits on the pair in 4 of 8 decisions in English and 3 of 8 in Hindi, the two never share an opening word or frame. Every decision has a decoy of the nudge's kind (a judging note beside a judging note, a heavy fact beside the hard fact, a warm Nani fact beside the reason that matters). Judging notes come from Nani (twin A's nudges and two decoys) and Mausa ji (twin D's nudges and two decoys), each voice the same in both halves of its twin. Rajan (moody in D1; the pill box in D7) and Ganga (the hard fact in D2; 'dodges work' in D8) each carry two nudges of different kinds; Dinesh carries 'lazy' and two decoy notes.

Against type (rule 11): the women's jobs are electrician (Uma), school van driver (Deepa) and photocopy shop (Mumtaz); the men's are tailor (Dinesh), tiffin cook who lost a bus-depot job (Rajan), primary-school maths teacher (Sunil), auto driver (Firoz) and cycle repair shop (Nagsen): five against type, two with it. No note gives a real reason for its job; the two reasons that matter sit only on the matters pairs.

Numbers (rule 14, 45): in every decision a player who goes only by the first number, or only by the second, must still choose between the equal two, and no other card ties the pair on either number. Bars sit at or below the pair (slept 6 or more for the turns and jobs; on feet 12 or more for the cots and seats). Cards that would miss a bar: Nagsen (D1, slept 1), Yasmin (D4, on feet 10), Ganga (D5, slept 2): two women, one man. The swap test and the always-the-woman, always-the-man test end the same because the two share numbers and only numbers count.

Kinds (rule 51): Split (first met here, its home world, with the moving hand), Spend checks (new, moving hand at D4) and Pick one: three kinds, two new. The pick ones fall back to back (D2 and D3, D6 and D7), which may feel like the repetition you named on 24 Oct; the bible's plan keeps them, and Believe and Rank belong to other chapters.

Gains and loads (rule 23): the night turns and morning jobs are loads, so they are Splits; the cots and taxi seats are gains. Whether keeping Nani's spare key and holding her purse are gains (trust) or loads (a worry) is written as a gain and waits on the five-player check.

Words (rule 62, 63; written to the proposed caps, WAITS rulebook Q14): story beats come to 118 counted words in English and 112 in Hindi, under 120. No beat over 20 or over 3 pieces; the longest spoken line is 7 words; narration at most 4. Decision screens count the question, the key, the slot labels and the button: 14 at most in English and 15 in Hindi (D1). Not counted: names, kin names, numbers and times; am, pm, रात and सुबह are counted. The top-bar clock is not counted, as in the scroll design; if it is, D1 runs over 15 in Hindi. Outcome beats at most 19 a band.

Hindi (rule 66): no line by, to or about you shows a gender. The checker will still catch these, for a native reader to clear: the 'who should' asks बैठे, रखे, आए, मिले, करे, सँभाले, समझाए, जाए; रखे and सँभाले in Nani's asks; यहीं (2.02), ख़ाली (2.27), नहीं and आएँ (2.33); and छोड़िए and कीजिए in your lines. The doctor never takes a gendered verb (डॉक्टर का हुक्म, डॉक्टर के बहुत सवाल हैं), so the job is not quietly made a man's.

You (rule 38): three 'You' bubbles (2.04, 2.17, 2.32), each one tap, the same whatever you pick, never naming a card person. 2.17 names only the job ('Cots, sorted'), WAITS options Q14. Nobody calls you by a family word (rule 8; WAITS rulebook Q7).

Household and voices: Nani asks every decision and is seen only from behind or off the panel, with her present-day face chip on every bubble (WAITS options Q11). Mausa ji, the bible's chapter voice, is painted face-on in two panels, tagged 'Mausa ji, Mummy's sister's husband' (WAITS rulebook Q11). Mama ji is on the phone in D7 but never speaks, since his chapter is 5. No household hand reaches towards you; the file and key lie on surfaces.

Paintings to add to the painter's glossary before any prompt (rule 30, painter-glossary rule): Nani's hospital file (a plain buff cardboard folder; back page plain ruled paper with no marks), her spare key (one brass key on a red thread), her cane (wooden, rubber foot), the folding steel cot with a rolled cotton mattress, the hospital wheelchair, the steel tea flask, the doctor's steel trolley of plain folders, the X-ray door with its unlit round lamp and blank cream plate, the taxi with a plain yellow number plate, the plain white cake box, a phone face up with a plain glowing screen. Card faces: Deepa, Uma and Rajan have Rukavat-style portraits; Ganga, Yasmin, Mumtaz, Dinesh, Sunil, Firoz and Nagsen need Rukavat versions of their faces, plus Mausa ji's present-day portrait and face-on Rukavat panels, all through the heavy queue and the close-up check for painted dots and lightened skin.
Phone fit (rule 41): D1 and D5 (Split) and D8 (Spend checks) show five cards; WAITS rulebook Q16 for the 360 x 640 Hindi screen.
Help line (rule 26): one help line for women and men alike in the '?' sheet, checked against the official source; not named here, never on a card or in a panel.
Six-player test (rule 1), predicted only: a night in hospital with an elder should pass for all six (Farida the nurse knows the ward from the other side). Readers decide.

Scripts, in this folder: ch2_milp3.py (the line-up and numbers search, with the rules it holds), ch2_check.py (rules 13, 14, 15, 17, 20, 45 on ch2_design.json), ch2_notecheck.py (rules 19 and 36), ch2_words.py (the counter).
